bib.title: Iterated Decomposition: Improving Science Q&A by Supervising Reasoning Processes

question: Can a human-in-the-loop workflow of inspecting and refining task decompositions of LM calls beat less compositional baselines on real science Q&A tasks?
hypothesis: Decomposing tasks into inspectable subtasks and iteratively fixing the failing ones (starting from selection) can beat less compositional approaches while keeping the process supervisable.
contributions: A review of the literature on process supervision, highlighting gaps in workflows and tooling
Iterated decomposition, a human-in-the-loop workflow for developing compositional language model programs
ICE, an open-source visualizer for language model execution traces
Case studies on placebo extraction, participant flow in RCTs, and QASPER NLP QA

method.summary: Five-step loop: start with a minimal decomposition, run on inputs with gold answers, evaluate, inspect failures in the ICE trace viewer, fix failing subtasks (decompose further, add CoT/retrieval, edit prompts), repeat. Applied to select-then-generate pipelines on three tasks; the main wins came from better paragraph selection (zero-shot perplexity cross-encoder) and few-shot demonstrations for generation.
method.task: Question answering over full-text papers (RCT placebo, participant flow, QASPER)

datasets.name: Placebo RCT set
datasets.size: 61 experiments across 47 papers; classification n=48, description n=20 (held-out test)
datasets.split: held-out test set; separate validation set used for iteration (size not given)
datasets.source: Gold standards written by two Surge workers, reviewed and finalised by an Ought worker

datasets.name: Participant flow RCT set
datasets.size: experiments n=50, arms n=50, adherence n=135 answers (56/135 with adherence info)
datasets.split: held-out test set; development set size not stated (n=9 mentioned for one failure analysis)

datasets.name: QASPER subset
datasets.size: 100 questions sampled from 5,049 questions over 1,585 NLP papers
datasets.preprocessing: Replaced cross-reference tokens (BIBREF0 -> [1]); omitted questions needing tables or figures

inference.samples: inferred: single run per item; no seeds or repeats reported
inference.prompting: Zero-shot select-then-generate prompt (Elicit); step-by-step reasoning prompts in placebo decomposition; few-shot demonstration prompts (positive examples only, randomly sampled from dev set) for generation; textbook-style and StatsExchange-style prompts tried but not systematically evaluated.
inference.retrieval: Elicit baseline: monoT5 ranks paragraphs, top-1 fed to LM. Improved: text-davinci-002 inverse-perplexity of 'The answer to the question is not mentioned in the excerpt', one threshold across all tasks (slightly favouring recall); multiple paragraphs above threshold passed in paper order. Placebo: pairwise paragraph ranking (rank-and-answer).

parameters.perplexity_threshold: chosen empirically, same across tasks, value not given
parameters.T-Few: Liu et al. 2022 recipe, prescribed hyperparameters, no separate validation set; zero-shot prompts left in fine-tuning data

other.ensemble_rule_placebo: Yes if either arms or paragraphs say yes and the other does not contradict, else No

metrics.name: accuracy
metrics.definition: Judgement that answer matches gold standard; for placebo description, a no-placebo classification counts as wrong

metrics.name: F1
metrics.definition: QASPER answer F1, and paragraph-level F1 for selection

eval.protocol: Fisher's exact test, answers treated independent (p-values understated); decompositions iterated on a dev set, reported on held-out test; no repeated runs.

prompts.purpose: Elicit baseline answer prompt (also base of perplexity selector, ending 'Answer: The answer to the question is not mentioned in the excerpt')

prompts.text: Classify whether the paper used a placebo or not. Err on the side of caution: If you are unsure, answer "Unclear".
So, to sum up, was this a placebo-controlled study? Answer "Yes", "No", or "Unclear".
Instructions: Enrich each Passage with the Context. (four examples) Context: {{ context}} Passage: {{ passage}} Rewrite:

results.table: Table 2, row Final decomposition, column Description (n=20)

results.claim: Final placebo decomposition raises classification accuracy from 71% to 98%.
results.setup: Placebo case study, held-out test set, text-davinci-002 + monoT5 baseline from Elicit; ensemble of trial-arm and per-paragraph classification

results.claim: Adherence accuracy rises from 53% to 70% with perplexity selection plus auto-few-shot generation.
results.setup: Participant flow case study, held-out test set, text-davinci-002; Fisher's exact test treating answers as independent

results.table: Table 3, row + perplexity selection + auto-few-shot generation, column Experiments

results.table: Table 3, row + perplexity selection + auto-few-shot generation, column Arms

results.claim: The decomposition transfers: QASPER accuracy rises from 38% to 69% with perplexity selection + few-shot demonstrations (F1 15 to 32).

results.claim: In the baseline, 51 of 51 adherence false negatives came from the selection step, so failures were in selection, not generation.
results.setup: Participant flow case study, held-out test set, text-davinci-002, baseline Elicit top-1 monoT5 paragraph
results.quote: all (51/51) of these false negatives resulted from errors at the selection stage

results.claim: With an oracle for selection, baseline generation reaches only 77% adherence accuracy, showing generation also needs work.
results.setup: Participant flow case study, held-out test set, text-davinci-002
results.quote: accuracy on the adherence task rose to 77%

results.claim: Zero-shot perplexity selection with text-davinci-002 lifts paragraph recall on adherence from 0.09 to 0.76.
results.setup: Participant flow case study, held-out test set, text-davinci-002; score = inverse perplexity of the 'not mentioned' completion
results.quote: from 0.09 to 0.76 on the adherence task

results.claim: Fine-tuned T-Few classifier reaches paragraph classification F1 0.77 against 0.10 for the Elicit top-1 approach.
results.setup: Participant flow case study, held-out test set, text-davinci-002; T0-3B with T-Few on weakly bootstrapped, expert-moderated labels
results.quote: F1 = 0.10 for Elicit top-1 approach versus F1 = 0.77 via T-Few

results.claim: Regex keyword decision tree scores 94% on placebo classification, nearly matching the 98% decomposition, but only 10% on description.
results.setup: Placebo case study, held-out test set, text-davinci-002 + monoT5 baseline from Elicit
results.table: Table 2, row Keyword decision tree, column Classification (n=48)

results.claim: Stuffing as much of the paper as fits (4096 tokens incl. completion) with step-by-step prompting scores 69% classification, 30% description, about the Elicit baseline.
results.setup: Placebo case study, held-out test set, text-davinci-002 + monoT5 baseline from Elicit
results.table: Table 2, row Stuff paper in prompt, column Classification (n=48)

results.claim: Pruning raised paragraph precision from 0.14 to 0.29 but cut recall from 0.77 to 0.54; answer accuracy rose only from 0.55 to 0.6.
results.setup: Participant flow case study, held-out test set, text-davinci-002, experiments task
results.quote: pruning improved precision from 0.14 to 0.29 while reducing recall from 0.77 to 0.54

results.claim: Decontextualization helped experiments and arms (0.65, 0.75) but not adherence (0.54).
results.setup: Participant flow case study, held-out test set, text-davinci-002; few-shot decontextualization prompt, not systematically evaluated
results.quote: 0.65 for experiments and 0.75 for arms, compared to 0.40 and 0.55 for the baselines

results.claim: Few-shot prompts built from expert demonstrations (positive examples only) improve adherence accuracy from 0.53 to 0.70.
results.setup: Participant flow case study, held-out test set, text-davinci-002
results.quote: from 0.53 to 0.70 overall for this task

results.claim: Information about adherence is present for only 56 of 135 arms (41%), so adherence is mostly a mentioned vs not-mentioned classification.
results.setup: Participant flow case study, held-out test set, text-davinci-002
results.quote: information about adherence is only available for 56/135 arms

results.claim: Press et al. (2022) report a compositionality gap of around 40%.
results.source: Press et al. (2022), Measuring and narrowing the compositionality gap in language models

limits: Process supervision here means the developer checking steps with gold answers available; no claim for settings without ground truth.
Small test sets (n=20 to 135); 100 QASPER questions; p-values assume independent answers and are understated.
Models are text-davinci-002 and monoT5; authors expect simulation-style prompts to matter less with instruction-tuned models.
Decontextualization context quality not systematically evaluated; textbook and StatsExchange prompts not evaluated.
Keyword regex nearly matches decomposition on placebo classification, so the task is easy; authors note it does not generalise to adherence.
Decompositions are simple; cost of many LM calls vs end-to-end not measured (distillation listed as future work).
Missing: temperature, max tokens, seeds, perplexity threshold value, dev set sizes.

terms.definition: a human-in-the-loop workflow that incrementally improves a task decomposition through error diagnosis and amendment
approaches to LM training and deployment that rely on human-understandable intermediate steps
the fraction of questions that the model answers incorrectly out of the questions for which the model answers all of the sub-questions correctly (Press et al. 2022)
